thread:
Aisha: quick pulse — ran the micro-batch canary this morning on pool-3. lowering base_coalesce from 2ms -> 1ms shaved ~9% off p95 on short prompts, but KV hit rate fell ~2% for <64-token requests. curious if that's acceptable tradeoff for interactive flows
Ben: nice. do we have the perf trace? wondering if the lower coalesce increased kernel-switch churn or just reduced wait time
Aisha: attached short trace snippet below (copied results):
```
config: { base_coalesce_ms: 1.0, jitter_ms: 0.6, micro_interval_us: 900 }
p95 latency: 72ms -> 65ms
KV_hit_rate(<64): 84% -> 82%
avg_tokens/sec: +1.3%
kernel_switches/min: 18 -> 26
```
Carlos: that kernel_switches bump is the red flag — looks like smaller windows are causing misaligned batches and more frequent kernel rebinds. when sequence-length distribution skews, we end up swapping to a different kernel for the tail and thrash the LRU on KV
Aisha: yeah. profile shows most of the extra switches at the 2nd chunk (mid-sequence). hypothesis: micro-interval too short relative to backend kernel readiness for long-seq streams
deploy-bot: canary deployed to pool-3 (canary_id=c3f2), started 1746012300, duration=10m
Ben: two proposals: (1) keep base_coalesce=1ms but increase jitter to 0.9ms to desync arrivals, (2) keep jitter=0.6ms but bump micro_interval_us -> 1200 to give kernels more time to finish priming
Devon: +1 for jitter tweak first — cheaper and often stabilizes batch alignment without hurting latency much
Carlos: also think we should add a small adaptive token budget gate: if queue token budget < 24 tokens, hold up to extra 0.8ms to favour KV hits. current threshold 32 seems high for this workload
Aisha: ran a synthetic with jitter=0.9ms + token_budget_threshold=24: p95 sits at 66ms (vs 65ms), KV_hit_rate recovered to 83.5%, kernel_switches down to 20. avg_tokens/sec neutral
Ben: sweet. can we roll that config to a 1h soak on pool-3 and capture KV eviction/sync metrics? also add kernel-switch histogram to tracing so we can see which models and lengths trigger thrash
Aisha: will schedule soak. adding trace labels: kernel_name, seq_len_bucket, batch_size. soak window 1h starting 1746015000
Carlos: small ask — when you capture kernel switch histogram, also capture per-kernel tail-latency delta (pre/post-switch). helps detect pathological swaps where switch cost > gains
Devon: noted. if soak looks good, we should bake jitter=0.9ms + token_budget=24 as a candidate profile and run against canary traffic for next 24h
Aisha: agreed. I'll post results in #eng-runtime with the soak summary. thanks all :thumbsup:
Ben: one more: add a regression alert rule for KV_hit_rate drop > 3% vs baseline for 15m. last time we missed a recovery window and it amplified costs
Aisha: added alert rule to the canary dashboard (alert id: canary-kv-regen-1746).
Devon: acked. keep an eye on tail-latency anomalies during the 30-45m mark of the soak (that's where priming noise usually shows up)
Aisha: will do. follow-ups: soak logs -> 1746015000..1746018600, canary id c3f2. next update ~1746018600
